lab08-s000.title: Before You Begin
lab08-s000.markdown:
**Estimated time:** 15 minutes
**What you will gain:** An evidence-based estimate of the capacity Harborlight needs, and an understanding of easily overlooked factors that can prevent a planning environment from working. ---

lab08-s001.title: What You Have Built and What Remains
lab08-s001.markdown:
You have a plan, a forecast, a profit and loss (P&L) model, and a canvas the CFO can read. Before expanding access, one question from Finance remains inevitable: **“How much will it cost, and what could go wrong?”**

In this module, you will establish estimation assumptions and use Metrics to check consumption across the entire capacity. To understand an individual operation's consumption, compare capacity metrics before and after the operation. For multi-user permissions, perform the actual operations with accounts for each role and verify what they are allowed to do.

---

lab08-s002.title: Estimate Harborlight's Capacity Requirements
lab08-s002.markdown:
Harborlight's planning team consists of:

| Participants | Number | Actual operations |
|---|---|---|
| FP&A systems lead (you) | 1 | Create and edit planning sheet designs and writeback destinations |
| Regional finance leads | 3 | Enter and adjust plan values, and submit approval requests |
| Corporate controller | 1 | Review, approve, and write back |
| CFO and executives | 5 | Open the canvas and view it using filters |

Because billing follows actual operations, map these participants to the roles corresponding to their actions.

| Role applied by operations | Participants | Number | Rate | CU hours over 30 days |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Planner** | FP&A systems lead | 1 | 847 | 847 |
| **Stakeholder** | Regional finance leads + corporate controller | 4 | 168 | 672 |
| **Viewer** | CFO + executives | 5 | 37 | 185 |
| | | | **Subtotal** | **1,704** |

Allow for supporting Fabric workloads (Fabric SQL, OneLake, and XMLA operations) by adding the **30% headroom** suggested in the official [billing documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/resources/billing-fabric-plan). This percentage is a guideline, not a guarantee; actual usage depends on the configuration.

**1,704 × 1.3 ≈ 2,215 CU hours / 30 days**

lab08-s003.title: Will It Fit the Capacity?
lab08-s003.markdown:
Capacity supplies CUs continuously, so over a 730-hour period it can provide **CU × 730 CU hours**. Compare requirements with availability.

| SKU | Available CU hours over 30 days | Harborlight (1,704) | With headroom (2,215) | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **F2** | 1,460 | 117% | 152% | Does not fit |
| **F4** | 2,920 | 58% | 76% | Fits, but with limited headroom |
| **F8** | 5,840 | 29% | 38% | Has headroom |
| **F16** | 11,680 | 15% | 19% | Has ample headroom |
| **F64** | 46,720 | 4% | 5% | Uses only a small fraction of total capacity |

**Under these assumptions, F4 is the arithmetic minimum; consider F8 if sharing with other processing.** One Planner alone consumes about 58% of F2. However, this table is a budget comparison for a hypothetical 10-person configuration, not a recommendation or guarantee that the actual workshop will run on F4 or F8. If all 10–20 participants create sheets, the Planner count changes and requires a separate estimate.

> [!NOTE]
> **Caution: This table uses the official documentation's 730-hour conversion.** The [billing documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/resources/billing-fabric-plan) describes a session as “30 days (730 hours),” but 30 calendar days are 720 hours. Here, we consistently use 730 hours to compare with the official CU-hour rates. Distinguish this from a table for exactly 30 calendar days. Check actual session start and end times in billing information for the target environment.
>
> **Align both time windows before comparing.** F4 can be expressed as either “14,400 CU seconds per hour” or “2,920 CU hours over 30 days.” These describe the same 4 CU capacity over different periods.
>
> Subtracting a Planner session's total of 847 CU hours from one hour's supply underestimates the load by roughly a factor of five. [Module 00](00-prerequisites.md) provides worked examples using both representations.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This calculation assesses the **consumption budget**, not processing performance. It indicates whether the 30-day total fits the capacity, but cannot guarantee that throttling will not occur at 9 a.m. on Monday.
>
> Capacity is also shared with all other Fabric workloads. The utilization shown here is added to existing warehouse, pipeline, semantic model, and other processing.
>
> Before deciding, consult the [community capacity estimator](https://community.fabricplan.com/capacity-pricing/) and validate against the official [billing documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/resources/billing-fabric-plan) and actual capacity metrics. Only successful automation jobs are billed, with the official notation **2 CU per job**. This differs from session CU hours, so do not simply add it to this table; check actual usage metrics.

lab08-s004.title: These Numbers Assume Everyone Uses the System
lab08-s004.markdown:
The table above assumes that all 10 users' sessions **overlap in the same period**. In practice, all five Harborlight executives may not open the canvas in the same 30-day period. A new session starts only when they act again. A Viewer who reads board materials only once a quarter has four sessions a year, not 12.

Estimate against an actual busy month, not an imaginary month when everyone uses the system at once. For a finance team, that is usually budget season.

lab08-s005.title: Does 30% Headroom Really Cover Fabric SQL?
lab08-s005.markdown:
This allowance also includes OneLake and XMLA, so verify rather than assume. The following hypothetical example uses **two databases: a collaboration SQL database and a writeback destination**. Official articles differ on metadata storage for new Plans, so inventory the actual SQL items and check whether this calculation applies to your environment. Assume **22 business days**, **8 working hours per day**, and a writeback destination online for **1 hour per day**.

| Database | Online hours | CU hours |
|---|---|---|
| Collaboration database used during planning work | 176 | 306 |
| Writeback destination: brief writebacks and one downstream read per day | 22 | 38 |
| Subtotal at minimum idle consumption | | 345 |
| Including 25% for actual query processing | | **Approximately 431** |

Of the 511 CU-hour allowance, about 80 CU hours remain for OneLake and XMLA. **These operating assumptions alone fit within 30%, but actual headroom is not guaranteed.** It depends on the 15-minute idle period, executed queries, background processing, and actual SQL item count. If the same writeback destination stays online continuously, the approximately 38 CU-hour assumption becomes approximately 1,271 CU hours, a difference of about 1,233 CU hours. That change alone exceeds the assumed headroom.

lab08-s006.title: Three Common Sizing Misconceptions
lab08-s006.markdown:
1. **Assuming a user who logs in only once is inexpensive.** Billing is for a 30-day session, not by the minute. An executive editing just one cell as a test starts a Stakeholder session.
2. **Forgetting that role upgrades during a session are one-way.** When a Viewer enters a number, they become a Stakeholder; the Viewer session is prorated and ends. A new 30-day period begins at the higher rate, with no downgrade until expiration.
3. **Spreading work across capacities.** The billing unit is tenant + user + capacity. If the same user works on two capacities, two sessions are created and both are billed.

One more point is easily missed: **when multiple workspaces share a capacity, a user is billed at the highest active role across all of them.** Separate workspaces do not mean separate billing.

lab08-s007.title: Pausing Capacity Does Not Reduce Session Charges
lab08-s007.markdown:
If you pause or delete capacity during a session, **the remaining CUs for all active sessions are totaled and added to your Azure bill**. Pausing does not defer the charge; it brings it forward.

The following actions do not avoid charges either.

| Action | Actual result |
|---|---|
| Pause or delete capacity | Remaining CUs for all active sessions are totaled and billed immediately |
| Delete a Plan item | Sessions continue and the full 30-day period is billed |
| Exhaust capacity credits | Sessions continue to be recorded and periodic billing continues |

Once a session starts, the 30-day commitment is established. Managing costs therefore means deciding who can start sessions. We will cover that later.

lab08-s008.title: Fabric SQL Is Billed Separately
lab08-s008.markdown:
Role-based rates cover only use of planning features. Each Fabric SQL database in the environment incurs additional **compute and storage** charges.

- **Compute:** While online, at least 2 GB of memory is billed, with automatic scaling. Compute scales to zero after 15 minutes of inactivity. The database remains online for 15 minutes after the last query, so even a short operation is billed for longer than its actual execution time.
- **Storage:** Billing continues **even while compute is paused**. It covers allocated storage and backup storage exceeding 100% of the provisioned size.

**Official documentation differs on where metadata is stored.** The [prerequisites](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/overview-prerequisites) and [getting-started steps](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/planning-how-to-get-started) describe automatic creation of a metadata SQL database. The [FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/resources/frequently-asked-questions), however, says that collaboration DB connections are deprecated for new Plan items and application metadata is stored in OneLake. Check creation dates and actual items in the target environment, and estimate SQL and OneLake costs separately.

#### A Number to Remember: 1.74 CU

A SQL database **reserves at least 2 GB of memory and incurs compute charges while online**. Memory converts at 3 GB per vCore, and 1 vCore equals 2.611 CU.

```
2 GB / 3 GB per vCore = 0.667 vCore
0.667 x 2.611         = 1.74 CU while online
```

A database sitting idle online **consumes more than a Planner session's average of 1.16 CU**. An idle database consumes more per hour than a person doing planning work. The database's 15-minute timeout helps, but Planner sessions have no equivalent mechanism.

| Assumed online time for one database | Approximate CU hours per period |
|---|---|
| 22 business days × 4 hours per day = 88 hours | 153 |
| 22 business days × 8 hours per day = 176 hours | 306 |
| 22 business days × 10 hours per day = 220 hours | 383 |
| **Continuous (730 hours, matching the official conversion)** | **1,271** |

Pay particular attention to the last row. Just one database staying online continuously consumes **more than one Planner session and about 2.5 times the entire 30% allowance**.

> [!WARNING]
> The worked example in the official [SQL billing article](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/database/sql/usage-reporting) gives a total of 5,483 CU seconds, but its displayed rows (1,566.6, 3,133, and 1,567) sum to 6,266.6 CU seconds. Because that total is inconsistent, this exercise does not use it. Instead, it estimates using the conversion factors in the text: 2 GB, 3 GB/vCore, and 2.611 CU/vCore. This estimates minimum consumption, not the actual bill.

#### What Brings a Database Online, and What to Check

Any query counts, not just reports. The two databases have different activation sources.

| Database | What brings it online |
|---|---|
| **Configuration using a collaboration SQL database** | Check actual reads and writes from viewing Plans, commenting, saving, and similar actions. Do not mechanically apply the same SQL consumption to environments where new Plans use OneLake |
| **Writeback destination** | Writeback execution and downstream processes reading its tables: Power BI, semantic models, data agents, pipelines, notebooks, ad hoc T-SQL, and others |

The canvas in [Module 06](06-intelligence-canvas.md) references semantic model values and input measures from From Sheets. Changes within a sheet do not flow back to KPIs through the writeback SQL destination.

However, **you cannot conclude that canvas interactions consume zero SQL**. SQL access may occur depending on the referenced model's storage mode and sources, collaboration storage configuration, and related processing. Compare capacity metrics before and after opening the canvas, updating one cell, and performing writeback to identify which operations use which SQL items.

In other words, downstream architecture lets you control much of the writeback database cost.

#### Compare Downstream Model Read Methods

This hypothetical example uses minimum consumption only. Assume **1.74 CU** while online and 22 business days. An Import refresh that brings SQL online for just 15 minutes once per day gives `1.74 × 22 × 0.25 = approximately 9.6 CU hours`. A DirectQuery report assumed to keep the SQL database online for 8 hours every business day gives `1.74 × 22 × 8 = approximately 306 CU hours`. This comparison excludes execution time, query volume, OneLake reads, and model processing; it is not a guarantee of actual consumption or charges.

Direct Lake's OneLake read path may avoid direct SQL queries, but check fallback and other SQL access separately. Also design the Plan's source model separately from the downstream model reading written-back planning data. Align region, contract, and refresh frequency, then estimate using the official pricing calculator and capacity metrics.

> [!WARNING]
> Pausing the capacity hosting a Fabric SQL database also stops mirroring to OneLake, so new changes are not replicated. The [mirroring overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/database/sql/mirroring-overview) and [mirroring costs](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/mirroring/overview#cost-of-mirroring) explain behavior linked to capacity pause / resume and conditions that incur OneLake replica storage charges, including while capacity is paused. Do not treat capacity pause as eliminating downstream data costs; check these separately from storage costs for the SQL database itself. After resuming, an administrator must check mirroring status and target-table synchronization before downstream read results are used. Verify free allowances and billing conditions against current official documentation, your contract, and the target configuration.

lab08-s009.title: Read Capacity Metrics
lab08-s009.markdown:
Fabric Capacity Metrics helps you understand usage on the selected capacity. Do not equate capacity-wide values with consumption from this workshop or a single operation. During evaluation, distinguish the target capacity, period, concurrent workloads, and related SQL databases, and compare with billing documentation. Do not choose an SKU or determine costs from a single point-in-time percentage; review actual usage patterns with the administrator.

1. Select the target capacity in capacity administration and open **Capacity usage report** → **See usage report**.

   ![Where to open Capacity usage report in capacity administration](../assets/screenshots/lab08/capacity-usage-entry.png)

2. If **Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics** is not installed, check that its publisher is Microsoft in Microsoft Marketplace before installing it. Follow the app's connection instructions and your organization's policies for connection method and privacy level. If a time parameter is requested, specify the target region's time zone.

   ![Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics app in Microsoft Marketplace](../assets/screenshots/lab08/metrics-marketplace.png)

   ![Microsoft Fabric Capacity Metrics installation confirmation](../assets/screenshots/lab08/metrics-install-dialog.png)

3. In the **Compute** report, select the target capacity and period, and read total capacity usage, averages, and peaks. Values are aggregated for the capacity and period displayed.

   ![Example Compute report showing capacity-wide usage; actual data area is covered by an opaque mask](../assets/screenshots/lab08/compute-capacity-example.png)

4. To investigate one operation, use non-production exercise resources. Record the period, capacity, and filters before the operation, perform the target operation once, then inspect **Items** and **TimePoint Detail** under the same conditions. Usage display typically lags by about 10–15 minutes, and new items may not appear until the Metrics app's semantic model is refreshed.
5. If needed, refresh the Metrics app's semantic model and reselect the same capacity and period before and after refreshing. The following screens show the model before and after refresh, and Items afterward. Refreshing the model updates report data; it does not rerun workload operations.

   ![Metrics app semantic model before refresh](../assets/screenshots/lab08/metrics-model-refresh-before.png)

   ![Metrics app semantic model after refresh](../assets/screenshots/lab08/metrics-model-refresh-after.png)

   ![Example usage in Items after model refresh; item names and actual data areas are covered by opaque masks](../assets/screenshots/lab08/metrics-items-example.png)

Compare before / after differences with the same capacity, period, and filters. Other workloads, delays, and aggregation granularity affect the difference, so do not attribute it exclusively to one operation. Do not copy real-environment values or account information into public records.

Metric and feature displays and availability may vary by region, tenant settings, rollout status, and preview stage. Check the target environment and current official documentation before adoption.

lab08-s010.title: Control Costs
lab08-s010.markdown:
Sessions arise from operations, but you can control who is allowed to perform those operations. Three tenant settings determine who can start higher-rate sessions.

| Setting | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Users can upgrade to a Planner session** | Allow or deny Planner upgrades for the entire organization or specified security groups |
| **Users can upgrade to a Stakeholder session** | Apply the same control to Stakeholder upgrades |
| **Show Oversubscription Warning** | Warn users before starting or upgrading a session expected to exceed capacity |

All three are configured at tenant level. **Per-capacity overrides** through Delegated Tenant Settings allow different rules for production and test capacities.

Get these two points right in particular:

- **Planner access includes Stakeholder access.** Allowing Planner for the entire organization also allows Stakeholder for the entire organization. Restrict the scope with security groups.
- **Users without either permission are not locked out.** They can open Plan items in Reading view as Viewers at the lowest rate. This is appropriate for many business users.

Beyond settings, keep these practices in mind:

- **Limit who creates planning sheets.** Creating planning sheets or changing their design triggers Planner. Other users can enter numbers, approve, and write back at the Stakeholder rate.
- **Create reports with the appropriate role.** Creating and editing PowerTable and Intelligence sheets are Stakeholder operations, not Planner operations. Planner is not available at all in Plan items containing only PowerTable sheets or only Intelligence sheets.
- **Look at capacity, not workspaces.** Billing is calculated and reported at capacity level. The “Planning” workspace shown in billing data is not a real workspace; it is a label for capacity-level values.
- **Do not concentrate too many users on a small SKU.** On F2, F4, or capacity shared with other Fabric workloads, active sessions may collectively exceed the SKU's supply. Enable oversubscription warnings and manage the number of users directed to small capacities.

lab08-s011.title: Check Tenant Settings
lab08-s011.markdown: Before the workshop, review **Users can upgrade to a Planner persona**, **Users can upgrade to a Stakeholder persona**, and **Show Oversubscription Warning** with the tenant administrator. Check whether permissions apply to the entire organization or specific security groups, and whether delegated settings override them per capacity. Before changing settings, agree with the responsible administrator on ownership and impact. Planner permission includes Stakeholder permission. Expanding its scope may allow unintended users to upgrade, so limit it to the required groups. Viewing the settings screen alone does not verify users' effective permissions, billing, or capacity performance.

lab08-s012.title: Operate Row-Level Security
lab08-s012.markdown: Even if the connected semantic model has RLS configured, verify each user's actual viewing scope in the target environment. [Row-level security in planning](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/planning-concept-row-level-security) explains that users not assigned a role see the union of data from defined roles. However, for a Viewer in the configuration used in this workshop, opening the Plan without a role assignment showed 0 rows and 0 columns with **Semantic Model Not Found**. Adding Build alone did not change this. An unassigned Contributor was also observed to see all data values after personally running **Intelligence** → **Refresh Data**, which differed from the documented union behavior. These are observations for a specific configuration and may not apply universally. Do not conflate Viewer, Contributor, and Member results; verify each permission level separately.

lab08-s013.title: Assign Regional Roles Explicitly and Verify
lab08-s013.markdown:
The instructor uses a dedicated exercise data workspace and sample model without confidential information. Confirm that Viewer test users do not inherit Member or similar permissions from another role or group. Open the semantic model in **Editing**, select **Manage roles** → **Create**, and create the following regional roles. Set a regional filter on each role's **Geography** table and select **Save**.

| Role | Geography condition |
|---|---|
| `Workshop_APAC` | `'Geography'[Region] = "Asia Pacific"` |
| `Workshop_Europe` | `'Geography'[Region] = "Europe"` |

Reload the model and reopen **Manage roles** to confirm that both roles and their conditions are retained. After saving role definitions, assign users as follows.

1. The instructor opens **More options** → **Security** on the semantic model.
2. Select each regional role (for example, `Workshop_APAC` and `Workshop_Europe`), add the exercise test user under **People or groups who belong to this role**, and select **Add** → **Save**. Explicitly assign learners to the role for their region.
3. Reload the page and confirm that each role contains only the intended members.

   ![Filter condition for the APAC model role](../assets/screenshots/lab08/rls-apac-role-filter.png)

   ![Checking test users assigned to the APAC role](../assets/screenshots/lab08/rls-apac-members.png)

   ![Checking test users assigned to the Europe role](../assets/screenshots/lab08/rls-europe-members.png)

4. Open the Plan as a Viewer test user and confirm that model actuals are limited to the assigned region. Record unassigned-user results separately; granting Build alone is not a substitute. Also confirm that broader permissions are not inherited through a group covering all roles or another access route.

   ![Viewer checking data for the explicitly assigned region](../assets/screenshots/lab08/rls-viewer-regional-data.png)

An unassigned Viewer may see **Semantic Model Not Found**, as in the example above. Review this example screen. If the actual environment differs from the material's expected results, the instructor must investigate before proceeding.

![Example of Semantic Model Not Found for a Viewer without a role assignment](../assets/screenshots/lab08/rls-unassigned-viewer-error.png)

lab08-s014.title: Recheck the Display After Role Changes
lab08-s014.markdown:
Do not assume that adding or revoking a role takes effect immediately just because the page reloads. In this workshop's configuration, a Planning sheet was observed to retain pre-change values for more than 120 minutes. After a Contributor was returned to Viewer, Intelligence KPIs also retained broader values for about 21 minutes, then returned to the assigned region's values after about 50 minutes. These are observations from a specific environment, not guarantees of propagation time or behavior for other operations.

1. After changing permissions, run **Intelligence** → **Refresh Data** using the learner's own account. An administrator's refresh or a page reload alone does not verify that user's display.
2. Until results match the new role, do not treat that user's display as the current authorization result. After revocation in particular, account for the possibility that old Planning sheet values remain. Administrators must separately verify other controls suitable for emergency access revocation and their propagation times in the target environment.
3. Use Viewer to verify regional viewing. Do not infer the same restrictions from Admin, Member, Contributor, or other accounts where RLS does not apply or permissions differ.

lab08-s015.title: Handle Regional KPIs and Comments
lab08-s015.markdown:
KPIs aggregating From Sheets input values may not cover the same scope as actuals restricted by model RLS. In this workshop's configuration, a From Sheets KPI was observed to show the overall value even while the table was filtered by region. For regional actuals KPIs, assign a semantic model measure (for example, `Measures Table → 2025 Gross Revenue`) to **Actual(s)** under **KPIs** → **Assign Data**, then verify results with each Viewer.

Before the exercise, the instructor creates an Intelligence sheet in the dedicated Plan, assigns the model's `Measures Table → 2025 Gross Revenue` to the KPI's **Actual(s)**, and saves. The learner personally runs **Intelligence** → **Refresh Data** with their Viewer account. Start the exercise only after confirming that the model-measure KPI is limited to the assigned region. Do not judge propagation to that user from a stale Planning table or another user's refresh results.

Example displays for this sample's model measure are below. In this configuration, the From Sheets KPI showed the overall **25.9m** in each region even when a regional table was displayed. Verify actual values against the target data model and user permissions.

| Viewer regional role | Example model-measure KPI | Example From Sheets KPI |
|---|---:|---:|
| APAC | 9.8m | 25.9m |
| Europe | 6.2m | 25.9m |
| APAC and Europe | 15.9m | 25.9m |

![Assigning a model measure to the KPI's Actual(s)](../assets/screenshots/lab08/rls-model-kpi-assignment.png)

![Example comparison of model and From Sheets KPIs as a Viewer with RLS](../assets/screenshots/lab08/rls-model-kpi-viewer-example.png)

In this workshop's configuration, users outside a region were also observed to be able to read another region's comment text. Do not put information in comments that must not be visible outside the region. If necessary, turn **View** Off under **Editing** → **Security** → **Roles** → **Item Baseline** → **Planning** → **Comments** → **All Sheets**. This suppresses comment display for everyone; it is not regional authorization. Hiding sheets or visuals in the UI likewise does not change authorization to the model or data.

![Setting to suppress comments across all sheets; this is not regional access control](../assets/screenshots/lab08/rls-comments-hidden-setting.png)

**Distinguish PowerTable security models.** The [current security settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/powertable-how-to-configure-security-settings) provide **Manage Access (Legacy)** for editing operations and **Roles & Policies Security** for Read, Insert, Update, Delete, and static / dynamic RLS. Enabling the latter overrides Legacy settings. Item Baseline, tables without policies, and Bypass Mode can allow broad access; do not assume defaults provide restrictions.

Do not equate SQL connection identity permissions, existing SQL-side RLS, PowerTable policies, and From Sheets references. Do not assume SQL RLS is automatically inherited per signed-in user. As in [Module 07](07-powertable.md), **test viewing and change scopes separately** as users A, B, and an administrator.

---

lab08-s016.title: Know the Limits Before Designing
lab08-s016.markdown:
| Limit applies to | Maximum |
|---|---|
| Sheets per Plan item | **25** |
| Visuals per Plan item | **50** |
| Writeback | 1.2 million cells per operation |
| Infobridge query | 10 million cells per query; approximately 10 million cells is also the guideline when appending multiple sheets |
| Bulk data entry | 10 million rows |
| PowerTable sorting, grouping, insights, and find / replace | 5 million rows |
| PowerTable Gantt and Resource layouts | 30,000 rows |
| Excel export (raw mode / label mode) | raw: 20 million cells or 1 million rows; label: 5 million cells |
| Automation chained-trigger depth | 2 levels |
| Automation database-trigger writeback | 10 records per trigger type |

See the [official limitations](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/overview-limitations) for Infobridge and bulk data entry limits. Limits also depend on client resources, capacity, XMLA constraints, and other factors, so these counts do not guarantee processing at that scale.

The first two especially affect architecture. Although 25 sheets may seem sufficient, creating sheets by region and scenario can bring you close to the limit. In that case, split across multiple Plan items and connect them with Infobridge rather than packing everything into one item.

---

lab08-s017.title: The Connected Planning Concept
lab08-s017.markdown:
The following is a future business vision, not a procedure for building actual Infobridge connections or measuring synchronization time in this Lab. Before adoption, check availability and behavior in the target environment with the administrator and current official documentation.

With Infobridge, Harborlight's three regional finance leads could plan independently without corporate staff having to reconcile their numbers. Each region manages its own planning sheets; Infobridge imports and appends them into one consolidated dataset. Corporate sheets reference those consolidated measures. When the EU lead increases the first-quarter budget, the corporate totals reflect it automatically. No manual consolidation, mismatched numbers, or 11-day wait.

That is the vision for solving the 40-tab Excel workbook problem. Actual connectivity and refresh behavior may vary by region, tenant settings, rollout status, and preview stage. Before adoption, verify the target environment with the administrator and current official documentation. See [Connected planning with Infobridge](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/iq/plan/infobridge-concept-connected-planning).

---

lab08-s018.title: Pre-Production Checklist
lab08-s018.markdown:
Before making the planning environment available to real users, verify the following.

- [ ] Creators have the workspace Member or Admin role
- [ ] Participant account types, licenses, sharing scope, and permissions required for model connections have been checked
- [ ] Workspace-level Private Link is not used; the current documentation's different support for tenant-level Private Link has been checked
- [ ] The semantic model is not in My workspace; although current documentation supports composite models, operation has been verified with the target storage modes, sources, and authentication configuration
- [ ] Required connections, authentication, and any gateway needs have been checked for the target source-model configuration, including Direct Lake and DirectQuery
- [ ] Stakeholders have agreed not to rename items: **renaming the workspace or semantic model breaks the Plan item**
- [ ] The writeback destination is confirmed as a Fabric SQL database and a format is selected (Long, Wide, or either "with changes" format)
- [ ] Ownership is assigned for the fact that **deleting rows in a sheet does not delete rows in the SQL table**
- [ ] Downstream reports reading writeback tables use **Direct Lake or Import**, not DirectQuery, so dashboards do not keep the SQL database continuously online
- [ ] Sizing distinguishes participant counts by actual operation, SQL item counts, the 730-hour conversion, and business-day assumptions; 30% is used as an initial guideline and validated with capacity metrics
- [ ] **Users can upgrade to a Planner session** targets security groups rather than the whole organization, restricting Planner to modelers
- [ ] **Show Oversubscription Warning** is enabled if capacity is shared

---

lab08-s019.title: Knowledge Check
lab08-s019.markdown:
1. A Viewer opens the canvas and enters a number in a planning cell as a test. How does billing change?
2. How does the official documentation describe data for users without role assignments? Did the Viewer observed in this workshop behave the same way?
3. A Plan item has 25 sheets and Finance requests another scenario. What should you do?
4. You create a DirectQuery report on the writeback table and leave it displayed continuously on a wall screen. What consumption could result, and what alternatives are available?

<details>
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. The user upgrades from Viewer to Stakeholder. The 37 CU-hour Viewer session is prorated and ends, and a new 30-day Stakeholder session begins at 168 CU hours. The user cannot downgrade until it expires.
2. The official documentation describes the union of data from defined roles. However, when an unassigned Viewer opened the Plan in this workshop's configuration, it showed 0 rows and 0 columns with **Semantic Model Not Found**. Adding Build alone did not change it. This is a configuration-specific observation, not a general rule for other environments. Explicitly assign Viewer roles and verify the actual display.
3. The per-item limit has been reached. Instead of forcing in another sheet, split into a second Plan item and connect it through Infobridge.
4. If the report keeps querying SQL and the database stays online for 730 hours, minimum consumption alone is about 1,271 CU hours. Whether continuous display means continuous queries must be checked through actual refresh settings, queries, and capacity metrics. Consider Direct Lake's file-read path or Import refreshed only as often as needed. For the Import example of once per day over 22 days, idle-period consumption is about 9.6 CU hours, with query execution extra.

</details>
